questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is best for showing individual values of one numerical variable?

feedback.text: A pie chart is for categorical parts of a whole.
A two-way table organizes two categorical variables.
Segmented bars compare categorical relative frequencies.
A dot plot preserves individual numerical values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display best shows the relationship between height and arm span?

feedback.text: Height and arm span are two numerical variables.
A bar chart compares category counts.
A histogram shows one numerical variable.
A pie chart shows categorical parts of a whole.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A histogram is most useful when the goal is to show what?

answer.text: The relationship between two categorical variables

feedback.text: That is a two-way table situation.

answer.text: The exact identity of every person

feedback.text: Histograms summarize groups and do not identify individuals.

answer.text: The distribution of one numerical variable grouped into intervals

feedback.text: Histograms show frequencies across numerical intervals.

answer.text: The percent of a whole for categories

feedback.text: That is a categorical display purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A box plot is especially useful for comparing what features of numerical data?

feedback.text: Category labels are not summarized by quartiles.
Two-way tables handle two categorical variables.
Pie charts show parts of a whole.
Box plots summarize center and spread.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A teacher has one numerical variable: quiz score. Which display pair could fit?

feedback.text: A scatterplot needs two numerical variables, and a two-way table needs categories.
Both show distributions of one numerical variable.
Those are categorical displays.

answer.text: Segmented bar graph or pie chart

feedback.text: Those show categorical proportions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which choice explains why a scatterplot is not right for one list of wait times?

feedback.text: Wait time is numerical.
Scatterplots use numerical pairs.

answer.text: A scatterplot requires two numerical variables

feedback.text: One list of wait times is univariate numerical data.

answer.text: All wait-time data must use a pie chart

feedback.text: Pie charts are for categorical parts of a whole.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which data situation best fits a histogram?

answer.text: Ages of 200 visitors grouped by intervals

feedback.text: Ages are numerical and can be grouped into intervals.
Favorite exhibit is categorical.
Those are categorical variables.
Two numerical variables fit a scatterplot.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display should be chosen for distance traveled and time spent traveling for each trip?

feedback.text: A pie chart is categorical.
Distance and time are paired numerical variables.
The variables are numerical measurements.
Trip names would not show the relationship between distance and time.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A dot plot is useful instead of a histogram when what matters?

feedback.text: That calls for a two-way table.
That calls for relative frequency or pie chart.
A dot plot does not prove causation.
Dot plots show each recorded numerical value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which statement correctly matches display and purpose?

feedback.text: Favorite colors are categorical.
A histogram displays one numerical variable in intervals.
Scatterplots use two numerical variables.
Box plots summarize numerical data.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which variable would be appropriate for a box plot?

feedback.text: This is categorical.
This is a label.
This is categorical.
Height is numerical and can be summarized with quartiles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display is least appropriate for one numerical variable?

feedback.text: Dot plots show one numerical variable.
A two-way table is for two categorical variables, not one numerical variable.
Histograms show one numerical variable.
Box plots summarize one numerical variable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A data set records temperature for each day. Which display could show distribution?

feedback.text: Temperatures are numerical values that can be grouped into intervals.
There are not two categorical variables.
Temperature is numerical, not categorical.
Segmented bars compare categorical relative frequencies.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Why should units be considered when representing numerical data?

feedback.text: Units describe measurements, not categories.

answer.text: Units determine the correct answer letter

feedback.text: Answer letters are assessment formatting, not data meaning.

answer.text: Units clarify what the numerical values measure

feedback.text: Units help the display communicate the context accurately.

answer.text: Units replace the need for a display

feedback.text: A display is still needed to show patterns.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which graph would best compare distributions of test scores for two classes using quartiles?

feedback.text: Side-by-side box plots compare centers and spreads.
Pie charts show categorical parts of a whole.
Scatterplots show relationships between two numerical variables.
Two-way tables summarize categorical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A scatterplot should be used only when each case has what?

feedback.text: Each point in a scatterplot represents a pair of numerical values.
A single category label does not create a scatterplot point.

answer.text: A count and a category only

feedback.text: A mixed pair may need another display, not a standard scatterplot.
Answer choices are assessment structure, not data structure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display would best show the spread of delivery times?

feedback.text: Pie charts show categorical parts of a whole.
Delivery times are numerical measurements.
A two-way table is for two categorical variables.
A box plot summarizes spread and center for numerical delivery times.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A student selects a histogram for favorite pet type. What is the error?

feedback.text: Histograms do show frequencies.

answer.text: Pet data can never be displayed

feedback.text: Pet type can be displayed using a bar chart or table.

answer.text: Favorite pet type is categorical, not numerical

feedback.text: Histograms require numerical intervals.

answer.text: The data has too many categories for any display

feedback.text: Multiple categories can be displayed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which question asks for a relationship between two numerical variables?

feedback.text: That is one categorical variable.

answer.text: What are the ages of students in class?

feedback.text: That is one numerical variable.

answer.text: Which club has the most members?

feedback.text: That is categorical count comparison.

answer.text: Does practice time relate to free-throw percentage?

feedback.text: Practice time and free-throw percentage are numerical variables.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display choice is appropriate for one numerical variable with many values?

feedback.text: A histogram can group many numerical values into intervals.
A pie chart is for categorical proportions.
A two-way table is for two categorical variables.
Labels are categorical, not raw numerical values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

What is the first decision when choosing a numerical display?

answer.text: Whether the graph will use blue or red

feedback.text: Color does not determine the appropriate display.

answer.text: Whether the data has a title

feedback.text: A title is useful but not the first display decision.

answer.text: Whether there is one numerical variable or two

feedback.text: One variable suggests distribution displays, while two numerical variables suggest a relationship display.

answer.text: Whether the values are written in a table

feedback.text: The table format does not decide the best display by itself.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

A line of best fit would most likely be connected to which display?

feedback.text: Pie charts do not use lines of best fit.
A line of best fit can summarize a trend in paired numerical data.
Frequency tables list counts, not numerical trends.
Box plots summarize distribution, not paired trends.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which numerical display shows every value as a mark above a number line?

feedback.text: Dot plots place marks above numerical values.
Two-way tables organize category pairs.
Pie charts show categorical parts.
Scatterplots plot paired numerical values on two axes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which display would not preserve every individual value?

feedback.text: Dot plots usually preserve individual values.
A data table can list individual values.
A histogram groups values into intervals, so exact individual values may not be visible.
A stem-and-leaf plot can preserve individual values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U01_L03_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.STQ.1

Which justification is strongest for using a scatterplot?

feedback.text: Category names do not fit a scatterplot.

answer.text: The data pair two numerical measurements for each case

feedback.text: Scatterplots represent paired numerical data.

answer.text: The question asks for the most popular category

feedback.text: That calls for a categorical display.
Visual style is not statistical justification.
